newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher amid firmer cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher amid firmer cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open slightly higher Friday amid early talk of firmer cash prices for the weekend, market sources said.
July over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.23 to $2.245 after settling to the upside Thursday at $2.221 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, July last traded 1.6 cents higher at $2.237.
Early cash prices at Henry Hub were talked at $2.24-2.27, up from Thursday's trading at $2.21-2.24.
Chart traders said July resistance was at $2.25 and then at $2.28-2.285 and $2.36-2.37. Support was pegged at $2.13, and then at $2.055 and $2.

In Wednesday's cash, Louisiana Gulf Coast gas firmed slightly to about $2.20. Midcon pipes were up a couple of cents to about $2.07-2.08. New York city gate gas was quoted about two cents higher in the mid-to-high $2.40s.

Supporting prices in the near-term, traders said, were forecasts calling for mostly above-normal temperatures across the East, Midwest and Southwest through early next week. Cooler weather is forecast to return to the Northeast and Midwest by midweek, Weather Services Corp said.
Traders also said electricity prices in the Southwest were sharply lower this morning in anticipation of the full return of El Paso Natural Gas Co's Blanco gas plant in the San Juan Basin.
On Friday and Saturday, 240 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of gas will still be cut, but on Sunday operations at the plant will return to normal.
The Blanco plant normally processes about one billion cubic feet per day of gas.
